sn1.20:1.5: The commentary says the deity is female, but he is addressed as _āvuso_ by Samiddhi and _yakkha_ by the Buddha, both of which are masculine.
sn1.20:2.3: The deity is playing with two meanings of _bhutvāna_. The obvious sense is “having eaten”, because one can only eat after going for alms. By reversing the terms, they introduce a paradox—how can one eat without having obtained food?—and thereby force the second meaning of _bhutvāna_, “having enjoyed (the pleasures of life)”. They are suggesting that the mendicant should enjoy sensual pleasures while young, then go forth.
sn1.20:3.1: Samiddhi joins the game, answering the deity with another play on words. He implies that “time” means the “time of death”.
sn1.20:21.5: Text takes these lines as verse, BB treats as prose; but they seem metrical to me.
